title: Bind NodeAuthority into GraphRevisionContent v3
description: OBJECTIVE: make canonical graph identity authenticate reconstructable NodeDefinition and dependency content rather than structural `{nodeKey,executionBearing}` rows alone. HARD DEPENDENCY: task-39c4bccda1d04279b844a92e5b17c429 must be DONE. DELIVERABLE: evolve the existing @moe/scheduler GraphRevisionContent codec/hash domain from v2 to v3 with a mandatory canonical nodeAuthority set returned by the production recursive derivation. The graph codec must validate the structural snapshot once, call the NodeAuthority production composer, bind every node and HARD edge exactly, and include the complete admitted authority set in canonical bytes and graphContentHash alongside all existing fields. Old v1/v2 or structural-only bodies refuse; no legacy fallback or caller hash. Update scheduler-owned surface/runtime fixtures in the same slice so the package stays green. NOT IN SCOPE: root-exporting NodeAuthority itself, daemon/store/transport code, or external security fixture migration. The publication/hardening task filed next consumes this v3 surface.
definitionOfDone: GraphRevisionContent v3 has a mandatory canonical nodeAuthority field/set; GRAPH_REVISION_CONTENT_KEYS, canonical serialization and the graph hash cover it together with the existing snapshot/base/parent/completion/policy/budget/author fields, and v1/v2/structural-only bytes refuse with exact unsupported-schema code+layer.

encode/decode call the production recursive NodeAuthority composer, require exact snapshot-node and HARD-edge closure, check completion/repository-base/policy inputs once, and never accept caller node hashes or a final-graph hash as a DependencyContract structural binding.

A nonempty multi-node control proves canonical round trip, full-byte graph identity and runtime Node strip-types loading; mutating each node field, direct contract, predecessor authority, advisory relation or existing graph field changes graphContentHash, while every negative path pins exact code+layer and nonzero generated counts.

The v3 integration preserves current graph-validation source codes/layers, rejects malformed/noncanonical/digest/binding failures in deliberate precedence, deep-freezes/detaches results, and keeps all production sources <=250 by refactoring focused responsibilities rather than appending past caps.

`pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` exits 0 with nonzero Test Files/Tests counts; exact runtime bridge behavior is exercised, no external fixtures are edited, and the task records the root-publication consumer id.
taskRails: Own only packages/scheduler/src/graph-content.ts, graph-content-fields.ts, graph-content-format.ts, graph-content-issues.ts, graph-content.test.ts, index-surface.test.ts, scheduler-entrypoint-smoke-worker.mjs, and scheduler-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts.
Bump the content wire/hash domain to v3 and fail closed on v1/v2; never silently upgrade or authenticate structural-only content.
The production call from graph-content.ts to task-39c4... output is the required consumer edge; do not copy its hashing or dependency semantics.

DISCLOSED, not hidden: the aggregate v3 ceiling is 64 * maxBytes, which a 3-node control cannot straddle, so the over-side of the AGGREGATE bound stays the existing length guard (Uint8Array(MAX+1) => TOO_LARGE@CODEC) and the straddle is proven per-body plus linearity.

GREEN part 2 — orchestration landed. `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` = EXIT 0, "Test Files 47 passed (47) / Tests 1553 passed (1553)" (baseline 47/1530). `npx tsc --project tsconfig.json` from packages/scheduler = EXIT 0.

GRAPH_CONTENT_SCHEMA_VERSION -> 3. New `bindAuthority(graph, fields, policyOverride)` is the REQUIRED consumer edge (task rail 3): it calls `deriveNodeAuthoritySet(projectGraphSnapshot(graph), definitions, policyOverride)` and COMPARES pairwise against the stated set. The composer's refusals go out through `authorityPassthrough` with code AND layer intact; only the disagreement is the codec's own verdict. The DERIVED set is what gets embedded, hashed and returned — the stated set is discarded once checked, so no caller hash ever gains authority. No node hash and no closure rule is reimplemented here.

WHY THE COMPOSER GETS `projectGraphSnapshot(graph)` AND NOT `read.snapshot`: the raw caller value has already been read once by the kernel, and handing it over a second time is exactly the accessor-drift hazard the field reader exists to close. The frozen canonical projection re-validates deterministically instead. Encode passes the caller's policyOverride, decode passes DECODE_POLICY, so decodability stays policy-free in both directions.

PRECEDENCE (deliberate, each arm pinned by a test). ENCODE: FIELD_INVALID -> validator passthrough -> COMPLETION_DRIFT -> composer passthrough -> AUTHORITY_DISAGREEMENT -> accept. DECODE: NOT_BYTES -> TOO_LARGE -> UNREADABLE -> MALFORMED -> UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA -> FIELD_INVALID -> validator passthrough -> COMPLETION_DRIFT -> composer passthrough -> AUTHORITY_DISAGREEMENT -> DIGEST_MISMATCH -> NONCANONICAL -> accept. The binding sits BEFORE the digest for the same reason completion drift does: a two-hash swap inside canonical bytes recomputes a self-consistent envelope, so only a decoder that RE-RUNS the composer can tell it from the real thing; a decoder that adopted the embedded set would report the misleading DIGEST_MISMATCH. Proven both ways — the swap arm demands AUTHORITY_DISAGREEMENT, and a moved v2 field (author) still reports DIGEST_MISMATCH.

DEEP-FREEZE + DETACH: the field reader already returns a JSON-detached clone, so `bindAuthority` deep-freezes that clone in place. Freezing the CALLER's objects would have made the detachment test's own `pop()` throw; cloning first is what lets the test mutate its record after the call and still find the answer unmoved.

REFACTOR NEEDED FOR THE 250 CAP, and a real improvement: `refuse(code, layer, message)` became `refuse(code, message)` with the layer read from a new closed `GRAPH_CONTENT_ISSUE_LAYER` table in graph-content-issues.ts. Every code this codec owns has exactly ONE layer; the binding was previously restated at 12 call sites where a typo could file a framing failure under the identity layer. A new test pins the table BIDIRECTIONALLY (table keys === code roster, every value in the layer roster) and cross-checks it against the pairs two real refusals actually carry, so the table cannot become a parallel opinion.
